newsitem.title: USA: Regulators back NYSE circuit breaker plan.
newsitem.headline: Regulators back NYSE circuit breaker plan.

text.p: Federal market regulators Friday approved a New York Stock Exchange plan to expand trading limits during periods of extreme stock market sell-offs, effective Monday.

The first trigger, which would halt trading in stocks for 30 minutes, has been increased to a decline of 350 points in the Dow Jones industrial average from the previous day's closing value, from the previous 250 points, the Securities and Exchange Commission said.
The second trigger, which would halt trading in stocks for one hour, has been increased to a decline of 550 points from 400 points, the regulators said.

In a statement, the SEC said that the rise in stock prices since the adoption of the so-called circuit breakers in 1988 justifies increases in the triggers to prevent "the premature application of the marketwide trading halts."
The new "circuit breaker" trigger level changes apply to the rules of the New York Stock Exchange, the American Stock Exchange and other securities markets, the SEC said.

The changes have been approved on a one-year basis, during which time the SEC said it will work with the markets to develop procedures to reset the triggers periodically to keep them in line with market levels.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission also approved increases to price limits and circuit breaker provisions of stock index futures and futures options contracts.
The new futures trading limits, which also take effect with the start of trading Monday, are being coordinated with the New York Stock Exchange plan.
